mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above the 5-year monthly average precedes a short-term decline in S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to tightened discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its 5-year monthly average
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not fall below the 5-day moving average during the trigger period, or FEDFUNDS remains above the threshold for > 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS (employment) coincides with stronger S&P 500 60-day forward returns as labor market strength supports corporate optimism and investment.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month period, 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant correlation with PAYEMS momentum (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in HOUST (residential construction) predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return via reduced near-term economic momentum and corporate caution.
candidate_trigger: HOUST month-over-month < previous month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 50 such HOUST declines in a 6-month window do not produce the expected cumulative negative return (cumulative p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in INDPRO (industrial production) below the 12-month moving average, combined with a simultaneous rise in GDPC1 (goods orders), signals supply-side weakness that drives negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average AND GDPC1 < 12-month moving average
regime_hint: Supply contraction in a growth cycle
failure_condition: No significant negative returns in 100 such events (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 5% for the first time in a 3-month window, S&P 500 20-day forward returns trend positive as low labor costs boost investor sentiment.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 5% over a 3-month window
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-positive in 80% of such episodes (rolling quantile).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising RSAFS (retail sales) above 2% suggests consumer confidence and supports positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS month-over-month > 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant positive returns in 40 such episodes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in CPIAUCSL (CPI) over 4 consecutive months indicates persistent inflation pressure, which is associated with negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL month-over-month < previous for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns remain non-negative in 70% of such inflation episodes (rolling quantile).

mechanism_narrative: Interaction between a sharp drop in GDPC1 (goods orders) and a rise in INDPRO (industrial production) suggests mixed supply signals that paradoxically drive negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns due to market uncertainty.
failure_condition: No consistent negative returns when the interaction pattern recurs more than 10 times (p > 0.1).
